The therapy is 131I on a polydopamine-coated PLGA nanoplatform delivered as local brachytherapy-style radionuclide therapy, "the direct local implantation of radioactive materials (such as 90Y, 125I or 131I-labeled microbeads) into the tumor", so it is radionuclide therapy but has no targeting ligand and the word radioligand never appears in the text.

The sonosensitiser and SDT are central: "greatly enhanced the HIFU ablation effects on ovarian cancer in nude mice by the HMME-mediated sono-dynamic chemistry therapy (SDT)."

A sonosensitizer is designed and tested: "a new sonosensitizer (Cu(II)NS) is synthesized... Through regulating the valence state of Cu, cancer SDT with enhanced therapeutic index is achieved."
Sonodynamic therapy is the studied modality: "immunogenic cell death induced by sonodynamic therapy and PD-1/PD-L1 blockade" via Ce6-loaded ultrasound nanobubbles.
The whole paper develops sonosensitizers: "ZnO quantum dots decorated BaTiO3 for cancer sonodynamic therapy... The work provides a guidance for sonosensitizers to tumor therapy".

The review's subject is SDT: "Sonodynamic therapy (SDT), which involves a synergistic application of sonosensitizers and low-intensity focused ultrasound to generate cytotoxic ROS", and its pyroptosis mechanism in liver cancer.
The paper builds and tests an "activatable SO2 nanosonosensitizer" in which "the sonodynamic, gaseous, and immunosuppressive TME reprogramming activities are precisely awakened under US irradiation."

SDT is a core reviewed modality (73 'SDT' and 40 'sonosensitizer' mentions): 'Non-invasive therapies that promote intracellular ROS generation, including photodynamic therapy (PDT), sonodynamic therapy (SDT), and chemodynamic therapy (CDT)... with a particular focus on the enhancement strategies for each therapy'.

SDT is the therapeutic modality developed: "a nanoparticle formulation, parthenolide/ICG-CaCO3@lipid ... has been engineered to amplify ferroptosis in tumor cells, positioning it as a potent agent for sonodynamic cancer immunotherapy."

SDT is a core arm of the study: "reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by sonodynamic therapy (SDT) promote effective drug release ... The combined SDT and chemotherapy treatment achieved a 94% tumor inhibition rate", using "the sonosensitizer Chlorin e6 (Ce6)" with 1.0 MHz ultrasound.

The validated assay was applied to "a clinical trial, which assesses sonodynamic therapy for HGG patients" and quantifies PPIX, which "is also used as a sonosensitizer in the experimental therapy known as sonodynamic therapy (SDT)", so it delivers sonosensitizer pharmacokinetics for an SDT trial (NCT04559685).

SDT is one of the named modalities the review systematically covers (54 mentions, including a dedicated treatment of "the sonodynamic effect of ZnO for deep-seated cancer elimination" and design factors that "may compromise the therapeutic efficacy of SDT").
The nanoplatform is built "as an effective sonosensitizer" and "under ultrasound irradiation, FL@M exhibited excellent sonodynamic effects", achieving "synergistic sonodynamic therapy/chemotherapy".

Synthetic lethality is the mechanism deliberately induced and measured, with a results section "Combination of ABT-888 with DETA stimulates synthetic lethality" and the conclusion that the combination sensitized "BRCA1/2-proficient cancer cell lines to IR through the stimulation of synthetic lethality".

The review is of PARP inhibitor trials premised on this mechanism: "Concurrent PARP inhibition in BRCA-mutated or homologous recombination-deficient tumor cells can induce 'synthetic lethality', which targets two DNA repair pathways."

Synthetic lethality is the therapeutic thesis of the review (8 'synthetic lethality' and 53 'PARP' mentions): 'preclinical and clinical data revealed a synthetic lethality interaction between BRCA2 mutations and PARP inhibition... Mutations in the canine BRCA2 gene have the potential to be exploited in clinical therapy through the usage of PARP inhibitors'.

Synthetic lethality is the review's organising thesis, in the title and the closing aim: "We also discuss the potential of targeting key UPR signaling nodes as novel synthetic lethal strategies in MYC-driven cancers".

Synthetic lethality is the studied mechanism per the title "Attenuation of SRC Kinase Activity Augments PARP Inhibitor-mediated Synthetic Lethality in BRCA2-altered Prostate Tumors" (MeSH: Synthetic Lethal Mutations).

Synthetic lethality is the paper's subject, not a mention -- "Here, we study the role of synthetic lethality in cancer risk" via genome-wide quantification of cancer synthetic lethal (cSL) gene pairs.

Synthetic lethality is a headline result with dedicated analyses -- "Synthetic lethality of Fanconi anemia genes in ovarian and breast cancer models", "Synthetic lethality in KRAS- and EGFR-mutant cell lines" and a "Pan-Cancer synthetic lethality analysis" -- not a passing mention.
Synthetic lethality is the explicit study design: "we extended our study to identify synthetic lethal mechanisms", with THZ531 plus DNA-PK or PARP inhibitor giving "synergistic cell death".

The paper is squarely in the synthetic-lethality lane, opening "The synthetic lethal association between BRCA deficiency and poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibition supports PARP inhibitor (PARPi) clinical efficacy" and dissecting resistance to the PARPi talazoparib.

Titled "The synthetic lethality of targeting cell cycle checkpoints and PARPs in cancer treatment", it reviews how "PARP inhibitors operate through 'synthetic lethality' mechanism with mutant DNA repair pathways genes".
Synthetic lethality is the experimental premise and conclusion: "our results provide a rationale to target DNA2 as a new synthetic lethality approach in mutp53-bearing cancers."

The paper's purpose is SL discovery: "we comprehensively analyzed large-scale CRISPR, shRNA, and PRISM screens to identify potential synthetic lethal (SL) interactions in pan-cancer and 12 individual cancer types."

Synthetic lethality is the entire framework: "This study aims to develop an interpretable AI framework for SL prediction and subsequently utilize it to design SL-based synergistic combination therapies", validated with the MDM2/CDK9 pair.

The study's core result is synthetic lethality: "Our analysis uncovers synthetically lethal associations between the tumor metabolic state (e.g., oxidative phosphorylation), driver mutations (e.g., loss of tumor suppressor PTEN), and actionable biological targets."

Synthetic lethality is the paper's thesis: "the cancer-specific synthetic lethality between HDAC8 and checkpoint kinases provides a promising replication stress-targeting strategy for treating a broad range of cancers."

A dedicated TPD review: "we comprehensively highlight the small-molecule degraders beyond PROTACs that could achieve the degradation of epigenetic proteins ... via proteasomal or lysosomal pathways."
The ADC payload is "a bromodomain and extra-terminal (BET) protein degrader named EBET", and the paper's conclusion is about "delivering BET protein degrader to PDAC and its microenvironment".

The payload is a degrader and degradation is the demonstrated mechanism: 'the bromodomain and extra-terminal (BET) protein degrader EBET... Mechanistically, 84-EBET degraded bromodomain-containing protein 4 in both cancer and stromal cells via bystander efficacy'.

The review contains a dedicated degrader section: "DACs utilize protein degraders as payloads instead of cytotoxic drugs", covering "Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras (PROTACs), Proteolysis Targeting Antibodies (PROTABs), and Lysosome Targeting Chimeras (LYTACs)" and E3-ligase-mediated ubiquitination.

Degraders are an explicit review topic, not a mention: "Novel therapeutic strategies, including PROTACs and metal-based agents, are discussed", with dedicated passages on dBET1, ARV-825, MZ1, ACBI1, EED/EZH2 degraders and CRBN molecular glues (34 PROTAC/degrader hits).

A clinical review of TTFields itself: "TTFields therapy involves a medical device and transducer arrays to provide targeted delivery of low intensity, intermediate frequency, alternating electric fields", covering the phase 3 EF-14 and EF-11 trials.
